claims.scope: Stabeno et al. (2016) report an approximate 1,700 km coastal system between Seward and Samalga Pass. This is the northern Gulf of Alaska/eastern Aleutian scope, separate from the offshore Alaska Current and Alaskan Stream. It does not cover every coastal flow sharing the Alaska Coastal Current name, including Arctic usage. The paper integrates intermittent observations from 1984-2014; this extent is not a measured simultaneous reference streamline or dated footprint.
claims.source_locator: Accepted manuscript, PDF page 2, Abstract, lines 25-28 (~1700 km, Seward to Samalga Pass); PDF page 3, Introduction, lines 51-59 defines the regional continuity scope.

claims.method: Intersect coast-masked approximate OSW state polygons and NASA's 70 published equirectangular crop rectangles in the same display projection, allowing 360-degree horizontal wraps. The overview is the level-1 crop with greatest display overlap, or level 0 if unavailable.

named_current_source_observations.spatial_basis: The paper identifies mooring arrays in Shelikof Sea Valley for the 1989 transport calculation. This is published local coastal-current evidence; no array endpoints, station coordinates, observed current axis, or footprint are digitized here.
named_current_source_observations.state_boundary_limit: ALSK is assigned by the source-reported northern Gulf of Alaska locality. This is a semantic regional association, not an observed-geometry intersection with the approximate OSW polygon; no BERS association follows from this observation.
named_current_source_observations.time_detail: Published Table 1 caption explicitly identifies 10 May-15 July 1989 as a sea-valley transport interval. The dates delimit this local calculation, not the full 1984-2014 study window or continuous coverage of the entire coastal system.
